explanation: Process count anomaly -- its own distinct attack type with its own UI feature, even though it also contributes as one of three indicators to the plain 'ransomware' entry's composite scoring. REAL ALGORITHM CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (2026-08-28), correcting the earlier QA-doc-sourced description: /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_98 stores a RUNNING AVERAGE (not a raw count) in /athinio/system/process_count.txt, updated on every run as (current_val + prev_val)/2, and a fixed timestamp in /athinio/system/prev_time.txt written ONCE on first run and never updated again. The anomaly check only activates once a full 7 days have passed since that FIRST run -- after that, it activates on every subsequent run forever (since prev_time.txt never changes, the 'time_diff <= current_time' condition stays permanently true). The real threshold is NOT a fixed number ('~50' as previously documented is wrong) -- it's diff = current_val - prev_val (this run's live ps count minus the PRIOR run's stored average) compared against current_avg = prev_val / 2 (half the prior stored average). Alert triggers when diff > current_avg, which algebraically means current_val > 1.5 x prev_val -- a 50% jump over the running average, the same multiplicative-threshold style used elsewhere in this product (config_drift's grace window, gateway_breach_activity's 2x average, Previous_Values.xml's 1.3x pattern). On trigger it logs 'Alert : Process count increased to N. Current avg val is M' to both /rationalVault/log/rationalclient.log and /var/log/osstatus.log, and sets <Process_current_value> to 1 in /athinio/system/alertlog.xml, which rolls up to Alert.xml's Process tag (confirmed present, currently 0/clean on a real hierarchy).

metadata.caveat: THRESHOLD CORRECTED (2026-08-28): the previously documented fixed threshold of '~50' (from a QA test spec) is wrong -- confirmed via secOpsScript_98's real source, the actual threshold is relative: alert triggers when the live process count exceeds 1.5x the prior stored running average, not any fixed number. Also newly confirmed: the 7-day wait is measured from this script's very FIRST run only (prev_time.txt is written once and never updated), not a rolling 7-day window recomputed each time -- once past that first week, the check is live on every subsequent run indefinitely. Like gateway_breach_activity, this needs that initial 7-day baseline period before it's actually meaningful -- freshly deployed or freshly reset, this will read 'clean' simply because there's no established average yet, not because nothing anomalous occurred. This is the SAME Process tag/mechanism the plain 'ransomware' entry treats as one of three composite indicators (alongside bin/lib drift, via a byte-for-byte duplicate of Alert1.sh called secOpsScript_99) -- checking this separately can surface a process anomaly even when ransomware's own 2-of-3 threshold isn't met, and vice versa; they should be read as related but independently meaningful signals, not duplicates.
